one_month_reasoning: Q3 earnings are scheduled for 2026-11-02, just outside the window, so no company print falls inside it. Events inside the window: (1) Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta Q3 reports in the last week of October. Their 2027 capex commentary is the main sector driver for AI-hosting names, which fell ~30% in a month on capex fatigue and credit costs. I expect capex to be reaffirmed or raised (2026 guides total $720-745B), a mild positive skew. (2) A possible new lease at Reveille or Ulysses: management cites multiple interested parties, and Morgan Stanley expected deals by October. That would be a +10-20% jump if it lands, but its timing is uncertain. (3) ERCOT/PUCT audit headlines (verification report due Dec 10), a two-way risk. (4) Bitcoin price and rates. Negative short-term momentum in the group (the stock fell from ~$18.4 on 9/25 to $15.46) offsets the event upside, so I stay near a symmetric lognormal centered at ~$15.50 with ~30% monthly sigma (112%/3.5 = 32%).

fair_value.method: 60% DCF/SOTP ($15.95 = $8.14 for the contracted 700 MW lease book at an 8.5% unlevered discount, rolled 12 months, plus $7.81 for pipeline NPV per MW) and 40% FY2028 EV/EBITDA ($733M x 15x less $4.23B net debt = $15.38), giving $15.72 on 439M diluted shares.

Contracted equity $3.16B gives $8.14/share 12 months forward. Plus pipeline: 477 MW x $5M x 0.7 and 4.4 GW x $0.4M = $3.43B ($7.81/share).

bear.story: The AI-infrastructure de-rating continues as capex fatigue, credit spreads and memory/semiconductor weakness bite. Barber Lake or Stingray slips, triggering overrun costs and talk of the 180-day termination clause. The ERCOT audit stalls the Texas pipeline and a dilutive equity raise funds the parent. The market pays only for the contracted lease book (~$7-9 DCF) and gives no credit to the pipeline.

base.story: Black Pearl and Barber Lake reach full rent by Q1-27 and Stingray starts in Apr-27, putting run-rate NOI at ~$800M. One or two new leases (Reveille/Ulysses, ~270 MW) are signed at rents near peer levels. Batch Zero clears part of the grid capacity in Apr-27 and the stock trades near DCF/SOTP plus modest drift.

bull.story: 700-1,000 MW of new hyperscaler or AI-lab leases are signed at rents at or above TeraWulf-Anthropic levels (~$2.4M per critical MW), with Google/Fluidstack and Amazon expanding. ERCOT confirms ~3.2 GW and the AI-infrastructure group re-rates toward the ~$31 sell-side consensus.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$9 the market would be valuing Cipher at or under my DCF of the executed lease book alone ($7-9/share), with nothing for 4.9 GW of pipeline. That would most likely mean the contracted cash flows are in doubt (an Amazon delay or termination under the 180-day clause, Fluidstack credit stress beyond the Google backstop, or overruns well past the $359M cap) or a deeply dilutive parent-level raise, rather than ordinary 112%-vol noise.

key_uncertainties: Whether the AI-infrastructure group's ~30% de-rating (capex fatigue, credit costs) continues or reverses; CIFR beta is ~3.2
Construction execution and timing at Barber Lake and Stingray versus the 180-day termination provisions and Cipher's $359M overrun share
The pace and pricing of new leases on 477 MW of cleared capacity; peer rents are rising (TeraWulf-Anthropic ~$2.37M per critical MW, B200 rental prices up sharply)
The ERCOT audit and Batch Zero outcome for the ~4.4 GW Texas pipeline
Parent-level funding: $1.47B of converts and equity needs for larger leases, so dilution risk
Tenant credit concentration: Amazon (AA-) plus Fluidstack, which depends on a Google backstop and its own $1.5B raise at an $18B valuation
reasoning: Start with facts from the filings. 700 MW of executed leases (two AWS, one Fluidstack/AI lab) carry ~$793M average annual NOI over 2026-36. The Barber Lake extension to 20 years lifted contracted revenue by ~$5.2B. Total debt is $6.0B against $4.56B of cash, mostly restricted for construction, and there are 415M shares. My explicit DCF of that book alone, including the ~$4.1B left to spend, is worth only ~$7-9/share at an 8-9% unlevered rate. So at $15.46 the market is paying ~$3.4B (~$0.7M per MW) for the pipeline. Industry evidence on that pipeline is mixed. Positive: hyperscaler capex above $700B for 2026 with 2027 guided higher; peer TeraWulf's 20-yr Anthropic lease at ~$2.37M revenue per critical MW, above Cipher's legacy rents; Fluidstack recapitalized ($1.5B at $18B) with a Google backstop; GPU rental prices for B200 rising; ERCOT Batch Zero pointing to up to 3.2 GW for Cipher. Negative: AI hosting peers (WULF, IREN, APLD, CORZ) fell ~30% in a month on capex fatigue and credit costs; the governor's audit paused new large-load energization in Texas; larger leases need parent equity. Valuing the pipeline at $5M per gross MW (70% probability) for the cleared 477 MW and $0.4M per MW for the rest gives a DCF/SOTP of ~$16. A discounted REIT-style 15x EV/EBITDA on FY28 gives ~$15.4, so the blended fair value is ~$15.7, essentially today's price. Sell-side consensus is ~$31, but it is evidence rather than the answer. For the distribution I use a lognormal with median ~$15.8 and sigma 0.78, below the 112% realized vol because contracted rent now dominates, but still wide given beta ~3.2 and binary leasing and ERCOT outcomes. Scenarios: bear $7 (25%), base $16.5 (50%), bull $30 (25%). Research was limited: Twelve Data fundamentals and estimates were paywalled, and Benzinga blocked fetching.
